title: Make scope trade-offs without losing the goal
summary: Every build hits surprises. When time runs short, cut or simplify work in a way that still meets the user need and the success metric, and make the decision openly.

beginner: When the team raises a problem, first ask what it affects: the date, the scope or the quality.
Go back to the goal and the main user need. Which items are essential to meet it?
Look for simpler versions of the hard parts, such as a manual step behind the scenes for the first release.
Never cut accessibility, security or legal requirements to save time.
Agree the change with the team, then tell stakeholders what changed and why.
Move anything cut to the 'next' list so it is not lost.
intermediate: Assess the impact of each issue on date, scope and quality.
Use the goal and metric to decide what to simplify or defer.
Protect non-negotiables such as accessibility and security.
experienced: Set trade-off rules with stakeholders before the build starts.
Spot scope creep early and challenge it with evidence.
Use trade-off decisions to keep the team focused and morale high.
Review trade-offs at the end to improve future planning.

canDelegateTo.task: Design a simpler version that still meets the user need
Show the impact on the plan

toolExamples.jira: Move deferred items to the next release version so the decision is visible.
toolExamples.confluence: Keep a short decision log with each trade-off and the reason.
toolExamples.linear: Label deferred issues and move them to a later cycle.

definitionOfDone: Trade-off decided against the goal and metric
Decision recorded and shared, with deferred work kept

leaderView.good: When time runs short, teams cut or simplify scope while still meeting the user need.
ask: What did we cut or simplify, and does the release still meet the need?
signs: Quality or accessibility is quietly cut to hit a date.
Scope never changes, so dates always slip.
